answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. The protocol links votes to that stake, caps influence per unit, and penalizes coordinated endorsements of accounts later proven fraudulent. Creating a thousand identities then adds little influence unless the attacker also locks a thousand times the capital, which remains exposed to slashing. A pulse of diverse activity may help flag collusion, but ivory tokens or orchard-themed profiles alone prove nothing.
